cases.title: Obstructed Corridor Egress Door
cases.user_description: Heavy stacked crates and packaging blocking the main emergency exit swing path.

ai_findings.summary: Multiple cardboard boxes and a large black trash bin are physically obstructing the path and swing radius of a designated emergency exit door.
visual_observations: A stack of several cardboard boxes of varying sizes positioned directly in front of the right-hand leaf of a dark gray double door.
A large black plastic wheeled trash bin placed immediately adjacent to the boxes, partially overlapping the door's threshold.
A green 'EXIT' sign with a running man pictogram mounted above the door frame.
A red 'FIRE EXTINGUISHER' sign and a red fire extinguisher mounted on the wall to the right of the door.
A metal horizontal panic bar (push bar) on the door that is obstructed by the proximity of the trash bin and boxes.
possible_interpretations: The items may have been temporarily placed there during a delivery or facility maintenance cycle.
The placement might be an attempt to utilize the hallway for temporary storage due to lack of space elsewhere.
unconfirmed_information: The exact direction and distance of the door's swing path cannot be confirmed without physical testing.
The weight and stability of the stacked cardboard boxes.
Whether the exit door is currently functional and unlocked from the interior.
potential_consequences: Delayed or prevented egress during an emergency evacuation, posing a significant life safety risk.
Increased risk of trips or falls in a high-stress or low-visibility (smoke-filled) environment.
Interference with emergency responder access to the stairwell.
ai_findings.confidence_rationale: The image is well-lit, in focus, and clearly shows the spatial relationship between the obstructions and the emergency exit door.
ai_findings.priority_rationale: The obstruction of a primary emergency exit is a critical life-safety violation that requires instant remediation.

verification_checklist.task: Physically test the door's swing to determine the full extent of the obstruction.
Check the stability of the box stack to ensure it does not pose a falling hazard.
Verify if any other exits in Stairwell 2 West are similarly obstructed.

recommended_actions: Immediately remove all boxes and the trash bin from the door's swing path.
Relocate the items to a designated storage or waste management area that does not impede egress.
Inspect the area to ensure no further obstructions are placed in front of fire safety equipment or exits.
ai_findings.suggested_report_message: URGENT: Emergency exit obstruction identified at Student Union, Stairwell 2 West. Multiple cardboard boxes and a large trash bin are currently blocking the swing path of the exit door. Immediate clearance is required to ensure compliance with fire safety and egress protocols.
ai_findings.limitations: This assessment is based on a single-angle photographic observation; physical verification of door mechanics and full swing radius is required for complete safety clearance.

cases.title: Severe Concrete Walkway Slab Heave & Trip Hazard
cases.location: North Quad Pedestrian Plaza, Near Library Entrance
cases.user_description: Uneven concrete pavement slab sticking up almost 2 inches along high-traffic student pathway.

ai_findings.summary: Differential settlement or tree root intrusion causing an abrupt vertical displacement of approximately 40-50mm between adjacent concrete paving slabs on a primary pedestrian route.
visual_observations: Sharp vertical ledge between slab joint sections
Spalling and edge fracture along the raised slab border
High-contrast shadow indicating significant vertical offset
Located directly along paved thoroughfare leading to public building entrance
possible_interpretations: Subsurface tree root heave from nearby mature oak trees
Soil erosion or freeze-thaw subgrade destabilization
Heavy maintenance vehicle loading exceeding slab design capacity
unconfirmed_information: Exact physical displacement measurement in millimeters
Presence of active underground utilities immediately underneath the joint
Nighttime illumination levels over this specific walkway section
potential_consequences: Pedestrian trip and fall injuries, particularly in low-light or rush hours
Accessibility barrier and ADA non-compliance for wheelchair users
Accelerated slab fracturing under repetitive pedestrian load
ai_findings.confidence_rationale: Clear geometric ledge profile, continuous crack line, and surface texture contrast.
ai_findings.priority_rationale: Active trip hazard in a high-traffic pedestrian corridor, though not presenting an immediate life-safety collapse.

verification_checklist.task: Measure exact vertical height delta with digital gauge
Paint high-visibility safety yellow warning line on ledge
Assess whether concrete grinding or slab mudjacking is feasible

recommended_actions: Apply temporary high-visibility warning paint immediately
Place temporary cone or ramp if wheelchair accessible detour is distant
Schedule concrete scarifying / grinding repair crew within 5 business days
ai_findings.suggested_report_message: MAINTENANCE REQUEST: Walkway slab heave of ~46mm detected outside North Quad Library entrance. Poses trip hazard. Please apply safety marking and schedule surface beveling.
ai_findings.limitations: Surface view cannot reveal root diameter beneath or underlying soil moisture conditions.

investigation_notes.author: Elena Rostova
investigation_notes.text: Gauge measurement confirmed 46mm. ADA threshold is exceeded (>6mm). Yellow marking scheduled for noon.

Electrical enclosure housing circuit breakers mounted 1 meter below seepage zone

Domestic plumbing supply pipe pinhole leak within ceiling cavity
Rainwater ingress from degraded exterior wall flashing

Whether liquid has entered the interior of the electrical enclosure
Voltage rating and live circuits fed by the subpanel

Unscheduled power outage to downstream critical server rooms
